Thanks @LuluGNavarro 🙏🙏🙏


Lulu NYT (@LuluGNavarro)

Watching @FareedZakaria and he talks about H.I. — Human Intelligence and its power to feel, to strive, to love and to suffer. A beautiful reframing of the power and value of the human mind.



— https://nitter.net/LuluGNavarro/status/2061099446155587773#m

At university graduation ceremonies this spring, commencement speakers have been getting booed for championing AI, given how the technology might threaten their job prospects.

In a commencement speech at Bard College last week, I delivered a more hopeful message — that humans can do essential things that computers simply can’t. Here are some highlights from that speech:

Video

I spoke with author @BruceFeiler about his new book, “A Time to Gather,” in which he argues that the cure to the loneliness epidemic might be found in one of humanity’s most ancient practices — ritual.

Video

The FIFA World Cup kicks off in less than two weeks in the US, Canada and Mexico — and it is already mired in geopolitical scandal.

So how much can the sport really stay separate from politics?

Guest anchor @biannagolodryga spoke with soccer-lover & journalist @ishaantharoor:

Video

Pope Leo presented a sweeping manifesto on artificial intelligence this week, calling to "disarm" the technology. What could this mean for the future of AI? Guest anchor @biannagolodryga spoke with AI ethics expert and Vatican consultant Father @paolobenanti:

Video

Has the US already lost the war with Iran? That's the contention of author and foreign policy analyst Robert Kagan, who joined guest anchor @biannagolodryga to discuss the the obstacles to securing a lasting peace deal on President Trump's terms:

Video

On GPS, at 10am and 1pm ET today on @CNN: @biannagolodryga will discuss whether the US has lost in Iran w/ @BrookingsInst’s Robert Kagan, the pope’s AI message w/ Father @paolobenanti, and the World Cup & world politics w/ @ishaantharoor. Then I’ll talk w/ @BruceFeiler about his new book “A Time to Gather” and give highlights from my Bard College commencement speech, all about the importance of “human intelligence,” not just AI.

On GPS, at 10am and 1pm ET Sunday on @CNN ...
• Has the US lost its war with Iran? Hosting the top of Sunday’s GPS, @biannagolodryga asks @BrookingsInst’s Robert Kagan to discuss the status of President Trump’s military campaign in the Persian Gulf
• After Pope Leo XIV issued a recent encyclical on artificial intelligence, Bianna talks with Father @paolobenanti, who has advised the Vatican on AI issues, about the ethics of this rapidly advancing technology
• The World Cup comes to North America

FORGET ABOUT AI -  LET'S TALK ABOUT HI
Commencement Address at Bard College piped.video/w8e35VtDMF8?si=-S3E… via @YouTube

Turkey has descended down the path of illiberal democracy over the past few decades. I talked to journalist @suzyhans about her new book that observes one neighborhood in Istanbul over a decade to try to understand the changes taking place under President Erdoğan:

Video

With such a challenging job market ahead of them, how are young people supposed to start their careers? I sat down with @jodikantor of the @nytimes who has a new book out to help young people answer that very question:

Video

Millions are graduating from college across the US — into one of the toughest job markets in recent memory. Is AI the culprit? I explored with @DKThomp, writer and host of the podcast "Plain English":

Video

Could economic concerns keep China from invading Taiwan?

In the second part of our conversation, I discussed whether access to Western markets could be a guardrail on Chinese aggression against the island with President Emeritus of @CFR_org @RichardHaass and former Singaporean diplomat @mahbubani_k:

Video

As Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin struggle through costly wars, in Iran and Ukraine respectively, what lessons is Xi Jinping drawing about Taiwan?

In part 1 of our conversation, I asked two veteran diplomats: @CFR_org President Emeritus @RichardHaass & @mahbubani_k of @NUSingapore:

Video

In his first term, President Trump was constrained.

This term, he has surrounded himself with people whose chief qualification is fealty. The result is reckless policy and the brazen pursuit of enrichment.

My take:

Video

On GPS, at 10am & 1pm ET on @CNN: I’ll discuss today’s great-power rivalries with @RichardHaass & @mahbubani_k, job-market uncertainty for new grads with @DKThomp, how those grads can find their life’s work with @jodikantor, and Turkey’s path of illiberal democracy with @suzyhans

On GPS, at 10am & 1pm ET Sunday on @CNN …
• As the US & Russia struggle through costly wars in Iran & Ukraine, what lessons will Chinese leader Xi Jinping draw about his ambition to take Taiwan? I’ll discuss today’s great-power rivalries with two veteran diplomats, @RichardHaass & @mahbubani_k
• Graduation day is a time to celebrate, but those receiving diplomas this month face AI uncertainty & a high unemployment rate among recent graduates. I’ll talk with @DKThomp, host of the podcast Plain En
Trump's 2nd term differs greatly from his first in a crucial way -- It is relentlessly MONETIZING the presidency.  washingtonpost.com/opinions/…

President Trump’s first term was more disciplined — not because he was disciplined, but because he was constrained. 

This time he is unconstrained by policy advisers, and more brazen in pursuit of enrichment.
